mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.25%) signals accommodative monetary policy that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.25% (p-value > 0.05 for positive mean return).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 5.0%, it indicates labor market weakness that typically precedes corporate earnings deterioration, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE > 5.0 (p-value > 0.05 for negative mean return).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both labor force participation (PAYEMS) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a broad-based economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in PAYEMS and INDPRO fails to predict negative returns in more than 55% of cases (p-value > 0.05 for negative mean return in the interaction condition).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising above 0.5% for 3 consecutive months), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to increased discount rates and reduced liquidity.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods during a monetary tightening cycle (p-value > 0.05 for negative mean return).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential construction permits (HOUST) above 1.2 million units signals strong housing market activity, which correlates with rising consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST > 1.2 million (p-value > 0.05 for positive mean return).

mechanism_narrative: When residential construction permits (HOUST) fall below 1.1 million units, it indicates a cooling housing market that typically precedes reduced consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when HOUST < 1.1 (p-value > 0.05 for negative mean return).

mechanism_narrative: During a supply shock regime (INDPRO < 105.0), a decline in industrial production signals reduced economic output, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 105.0 (p-value > 0.05 for negative mean return).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in residential construction (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a weakening consumer sector, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative returns in more than 55% of cases (p-value > 0.05 for negative mean return in the interaction condition).
